spec.title: OpenWrt - Topology
spec.description: Network topology node graph for OpenWrt: internet, modem, gateway, switch ports, access points, BSSIDs, and client identity, driven by the Prometheus datasource with no plugin install.

options.content:
## Network topology
internet -> modem -> gateway -> switch port / AP -> BSSID -> client, built from the same identity data as the clients dashboard. Node and edge frames come from the same scrape (topology.lua), so a client that disappears never leaves a dangling edge. Every exporter contributes only what it can see first-hand: a downstream AP never invents an uplink, and only the gateway names clients, because only the gateway runs DHCP.

spec.title: Topology Collector
spec.description: Collector availability gated by both the topology flag and the Lua exporter's per-collector scrape success.

spec.title: Nodes
spec.description: Nodes actually rendered, after cross-router reconciliation: placeholder duplicates and routers appearing as each other's clients are already removed.

spec.title: Online Clients
spec.description: Client nodes currently reporting arc__online=1, counted from first-hand series only so a placeholder never double-counts.

spec.expr: count(openwrt_topology_node{job="openwrt", router=~"$router", id=~"client:.+", arc__online="1", authority="1"}) or vector(0)

spec.title: Access Points
spec.description: Boxes broadcasting at least one BSS, including the gateway when it also serves wifi.

spec.title: Broadcast BSSIDs
spec.description: Distinct basic service sets. Two APs broadcasting one SSID are two BSSIDs on two channels, which is why they are separate nodes.

spec.title: Weak Wi-Fi Links
spec.description: Associations below -72 dBm. The collector colours each association edge from the signal it reads in the same scrape, so this counts exactly what the graph draws red.

spec.title: Offline Clients
spec.description: Known clients not currently reachable. Grey rather than red on the graph: a device that has gone home is not a fault.

spec.expr: count(openwrt_topology_node{job="openwrt", router=~"$router", id=~"client:.+", arc__offline="1", authority="1"}) or vector(0)

spec.title: Network Topology
spec.description: The live network graph. Node and edge values are current throughput in bytes/sec, joined from the per-device traffic counters onto the topology frames; anything with no traffic reads a truthful 0 B/s rather than disappearing, and routers without the traffic profile contribute a real 0 rather than a gap. The ring around each node is its health arc: green online/ok, grey offline, yellow warning. Association edges are coloured by signal - green above -60 dBm, orange to -72, red below - and a wired client sits under the switch port its MAC was learned on. Click any node for its client or router dashboard.

options.content: **Reading the graph.** `internet` -> `modem:` (only when the WAN nexthop is a private address, i.e. double NAT) -> `router:<lan-ip>` -> `port:` switch ports and `ap:` access points -> `bss:<bssid>` -> `client:<mac>`. Nodes are keyed so that every router names the same thing identically: the gateway by its LAN IP, each radio by its BSSID. An isolated client node means its connection state is genuinely unknown (no association list available) - the collector never guesses a wired link.

## Data quality
Raw, un-reconciled node and edge series -- what the exporters actually emitted, including anything the Topology tab is hiding. The three checks below are the invariants that decide whether the panel renders at all: a dangling edge endpoint crashes Grafana's node graph rather than degrading, and two boxes claiming the same id first-hand means one of them silently overwrites the other.

spec.title: Colliding Node IDs
spec.description: Node ids claimed first-hand by more than one router. Must be zero: Grafana keys nodes by id and silently keeps whichever row arrives last. Two gateways on one LAN is the realistic way to trip this.

spec.expr: count(count by (id) (openwrt_topology_node{job="openwrt", router=~"$router", authority="1"}) > 1) or vector(0)

spec.title: Topology Nodes
spec.description: One row per emitted openwrt_topology_node series, before reconciliation. `authority` shows which box observed the node first-hand; duplicate ids across routers are expected here and resolved on the Topology tab.

spec.title: Topology Edges
spec.description: One row per emitted openwrt_topology_edge series, before reconciliation. Every source/target must match an id in the nodes table above.

spec.title: Infrastructure MACs
spec.description: Each exporter's own interface MACs. These are why an access point no longer renders as a laptop hanging off the gateway: the matching client node and every edge pointing at it are suppressed on the Topology tab.
